typeIdent.description:
Indicates explicit sub-type of entry.  Composed of the concatenation of the typeKey of the instance's type and all
of its base type's typeIdent

id.description:
A unique identifier that can be manually assigned or generated automatically during object creation. This
identifier cannot be altered after the object has been persisted.

version.description:
Version number used for optimistic concurrency.  Automatically managed by the system.

Updating an Obj with a null or 0 value for version will cause the concurrency check to be skipped and should only
be done with great caution.

typeWithBindings.description: Persists concrete type with bindings for generic types where instance has parameter bindings

dataType.description:
The kind of data source. Example data sources are:
1. `SENSOR_TIME_SERIES` --> Contains time series data for sensors in the canonical format
2. `ASSET_HIERARCHY_EXCEL` --> Contains the asset hierarchy, asset class, failure mode,
and recommended actions in a single excel spreadsheet
3. etc. Look at {@link ReliabilityRawDataValidationDataType} for more information on the different
kinds of raw data sources supported.

file.description: A link to the raw source data {@link File} that is being checked for data quality.

errors.description:
For the {@link file} corresponding to the {@link dataType}, there are certain characteristics
that need to be present in the data. If they are not present in the data, all the erroneous aspects
of data quality will be stored in this field. If there are {@link errors} in the {@link file}, then
no {@link stats} will be computed since these statistics may be wrong.

warnings.description:
If there are any warnings related to data quality in the {@link file}, those will be raised here.
Warnings don't block the system for computing the relevant {@link stats} for this {@link file}. They can
be thought of as issues about the data that are nice to fix, not necessary to fix.
An example warning could be that there is no asset class information in the asset hierarchy excel
spreadsheet. While it is great to organize the hierarchy into templates, it is not needed for the
application to function.

stats.description:
Relevant statistics computed on the data in the {@link file} for its {@link dataType}. The kind
of statistics change with the {@link dataType}. But they are all stored as a json {@link File}. These
statistics will be cross-referenced by {@link ReliabilityRawDataValidationHelper#crossValidateReports}.

job.description:
It is highly recommended that the raw data validation be executed as a distributed
{@link ReliabilityRawDataValidationJob}. In the case that this report is generated by the job,
the reference to the job will be stored in the {@link job} field.

title:
This is a report on the quality of data present in a single raw data {@link File}.
If there are errors in the raw data, they will be recorded in the {@link errors} field. In this case,
no {@link stats} will be computed.
If there are warnings, they will be recorded in the {@link warnings} field. {@link stats} will still
be computed.
name: ReliabilityRawDataValidationFileReport
